notes: Direct translation. RL2's ex:use becomes odrl:use, as the attestation-gating case maps ex:read to odrl:read; narrower ODRL actions then match through ODRL's own odrl:includedIn hierarchy, which travels with every policy in the corpus closure (profiles/odrl-actions.ttl, due2-profiles.md §6). RL2's context.recipient.class is an assembler-supplied fact about the recipient, so it binds to the state source; due2-core's odrl:recipient (a request-source IRI) is not used because the policy tests the recipient's class, not its identity. RL2's "external" sentence becomes scenario 2. Scenarios 3 and 4 are added: a missing recipient class, and a narrower action matched through the shipped action hierarchy, with no SOTW closure edge: an action hierarchy is policy-side data, not a fact about the world (due2-workflows.md §3.1, §3.3).

expected.why: "internal" = "internal", so ex:internalUse is T; it has no duties and nothing prohibits.
"external" = "internal" is F, so the permission is F. The policy has no prohibition, so external use is not authorised but not denied either.
The recipient class is missing, so the constraint and the permission are U; the completions give Permit and NotApplicable.

scenarios.name: narrower action through the action closure

expected.why: odrl:read ⊑ odrl:use by the corpus closure (profiles/odrl-actions.ttl), so the action part is T; with the recipient internal the permission is T and has no duties.
